utterances.text: Now you asked the question well. A moment before, I think you tried to trick me which is not fair. I already said that Mr. Delalic did not take part in the take-over of Celebici barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, I'm just trying to ask questions so that the judges can evaluate what the truth is. I'm asking the questions as best I can and I just ask you to answer them fairly and as best you can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This is your intent. He said he did not take part.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: When I asked him was correct -- well, let me just ask him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Don't ask him that. He has answered the question that he did not take part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He said that he was not present at the time of the take-over, so how does he know who was present there or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: And the reports to him by his operations officer did not indicate that he took part. This is what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: If I'm not allowed to explore it, I will move on, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You can explore it if it's relevant. He said he was not present on the occasion. His chief of staff, Cerovac, was present, so the person to answer that question is Cerovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He has answered that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, but this witness has testified about it in direct and to the extent there's a discrepancy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You are wasting the time of the court. Go ahead and ask other questions, if any. If a question has been answered, don't go further, except if it is ambiguous, and this was not ambiguous.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: If Your Honours direct me to go forward, I will go forward.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, with respect to the document you were shown, your authorisation which was signed by the HVO commander, at the time that you received that authorisation to travel, was the joint command in existence at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Why didn't the joint command sign your authorisation, sir, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I received permission for private affairs from my superior command, that is, the TO headquarters in Konjic. In order to cross over the territory controlled by the HVO, on the basis of my previous permit, a separate permit was issued to me by the HVO. Without their permission, I would not be able to move around in the territory controlled by the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: So you had two permits, one from the TO commander and one from the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The permit which I received from my own commander I had to turn in at the HVO headquarters, and there I received a permit to move freely in the area under their control.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, during the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think we'll break now and reassemble at 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.03 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Are you finished with the research of the witness' background?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I was able to do as much as I could during the lunch hour, which was of assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may. You may note that the witness is still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This is what you should try and remember each time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, you were shown a document, D-176, a travel authorisation that you brought with you to The Hague, do you know where the original to that document is, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not getting the interpretation quite well. I didn't hear the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly repeat it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, you were shown during direct examination, a document, D -- can you hear me now, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: You were shown a document, D-176, a travel authorisation that you brought with you to The Hague. Sir, do you know where the original of that document is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The original is at my home.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Did you bring any other documents to The Hague with you, dealing with the situation in Konjic in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only brought a statement, the statement I made for The Hague tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Is that a statement you made to the office of the Prosecutor or to the Defence, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a statement that I made to the office of the Prosecutor and I did not give any statement to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, sir, on a different matter, did I understand you correctly to state that Mr. Delalic was never a member of the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you understood me well. Mr. Delalic was not a member of the Territorial Defence, nor could he be mobilised at the time I was there because, according to the law, any person who was absent for more than a month or two would be removed from the list, from the records, and would no longer be subject to mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, sir, are you stating that if someone came, a Bosnian citizen, and wanted to volunteer for the TO, he would not be permitted to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic was a citizen and an inhabitant of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but he was not on the conscription list because he didn't have any call-up papers because, according to our documents, he could not be called up because he wasn't there. He wasn't in Yugoslavia, he wasn't in Bosnia-Herzegovina and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, my specific question was, is it your testimony that if someone who was a Bosnian citizen wanted to volunteer for the TO, if he wasn't on the mobilisation list, he would not be permitted to become a member of the TO? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Is this a follow-up of the question whether Delalic was a member?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He could volunteer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That's quite a different situation from calling up somebody who is under obligation to serve.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do understand that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, sir, do you know, and I am talking about the time before he became commander of Tactical Group 1, did Mr. Delalic ever volunteer to become a member of the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And before he became commander of Tactical Group 1, did Mr. Delalic, to your knowledge, have any military function or duties at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: What was Mr. Delalic's role during the Oranj Operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Regarding the Oranj Operation, though I was a member of the staff, I did not participate in the planning and organisation or preparation of that operation. It was an operation that was conducted on the ground and we had a stationary system of anti-aircraft defence, which I was involved with and this was my permanent task and that was my task before the operation, during the operation and after the operation. So that it was a permanent duty that I had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The question was, what was the role of Delalic during that operation, not your own.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't know and I don't know the situation as regards to any role that he may have had in that operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, sir, am I correct that during the time that he was coordinator, according to your understanding, Mr. Delalic did not report to the war presidency?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How would he know?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think he has made a statement to that effect previously, so I am asking him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He made a statement to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: The witness has previously made statements about these things, which would indicate to me that he does have some knowledge. Obviously, Your Honour, if he doesn't have any knowledge, he can say, "I don't know".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. What is the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, am I correct that during the time that he was coordinator, according to your understanding, Mr. Delalic did not report to the war presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not a member of the war presidency, nor could I be present to be able to claim that he made any statements or reported to the war presidency. Therefore, I have no personal knowledge of that and there's nothing I can say about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with me that previously, when you spoke with the Office of the Prosecutor, you specifically reported that Mr. Delalic did not report to the war presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is true that he did not report to the war presidency at the meetings that I attended.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, sir, would you agree that in May and June of 1992, the Bosnian army or the TO was not very organised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Regarding the process of organisation and formation of the Territorial Defence, in view of the fact that we had to start from scratch, and that the process required a considerable amount of time, in some countries it takes much longer to form an army. Regarding the period you're referring to, the period of May and June, it is natural that the situation could not be organised perfectly, nor could it function perfectly. Similar problems occur in many other armies and, therefore, in our own as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I take it, then, that the answer is, "yes", you would agree with me that for the reasons you've just explained, the army was not very organised during that period?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Perhaps you're talking from different angles. Probably you're talking about organisation. He's probably thinking of battalions, command structure in the sense, but that there were no battalions, there were no brigades, something like that. Maybe you're talking from different angles all together.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's open for interpretation, but the witness did agree with me and I am just trying to get a simple yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Given what respect, from your angle or from his angle? And certainly the army could take much longer from side of organise. He's probably thinking of terms of brigades, corps, in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with me that in May and June of 1992, the structure of the Bosnian army was not very organised because it was in the process of being created?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The army was in the process of being created, but even in that process, the organisation functioned, which made for steady and constant progress and development. Therefore, it acted as an organised whole, regardless of the problems we encountered.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, after you stepped down as TO commander, in other words, when you were just involved in the anti-aircraft defence, did you have occasion to see orders signed by the joint command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some orders, which were addressed to me, I did see. But the orders that were not submitted to me and which I didn't have to receive, I probably didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: May I ask that the witness be shown a copy of Prosecution Exhibit 210. And I'll ask that the English, with the usher's assistance, if the English could be put on the ELMO and the Bosnian version given to the witness. Now, sir, before you -- before I ask you about the document, is it the case that you ever saw documents signed by the joint command or the head of the TO and also signed by Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document does not originate from the joint command. This document comes from the municipal staff of the TO. On this document we can see --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Let me just ask you, have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Have you looked at the date of the documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, 24th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What capacity do you think he would have seen it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it's directed to him with a copy to him, so let me just ask, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, in 1992, did you ever see this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see this document. I did not receive this document. But, if I need to answer any questions about it, I would be glad to.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, sir, did you -- was there ever any change in your duties as is reflected in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You didn't ask me a proper question, was there a change in my duties?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, sir, was there ever a change in your duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were no changes, I continued to engage in anti-aircraft defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you specifically, sir, was -- is your title head of air defence when you first -- what was your title when you first stepped down as TO commander, within the TO staff, what was your title?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Within the Territorial Defence staff, I held the position of officer in the joint command that is head of anti-air defences. In view of the fact that there was a shortage of such personnel, I continued to perform the duty of leader of the anti-aircraft battery.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And was there a time when you stopped fulfilling one or both of those functions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stopped performing the function in the municipal staff. That is the function of head of anti-air defence and I was appointed to the position of officer, in other words, an assistant.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And when, approximately, did that change in function occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Did you ask me until when?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: No, approximately, when was it that you stopped performing the function of head of anti-air defence and became the assistant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly the date, but if this document, if this paper is a document, then it could have happened in the month of July, but I cannot recall myself, the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, do I understand that the -- you are familiar with the contents of this document, but you never saw the document itself, is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remained head of anti-air defences in the joint command. And my duty of officer for anti-air defence and unit leader remained in the municipal staff. I continue to hold that post.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, I don't understand. Would you agree with me that this document, what is stated in this document reflects the reality of what happened? In other words, you, you were no longer, within the headquarters of the TO, head of air defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The witness has answered the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I continued to hold the duty of head of anti-air defence in the joint command. And this is a function that meant that I had competencies both over the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Croatian defence council. And I needed somebody to assist me in performing these duties as I couldn't cover it all, another person was appointed, his name is Esad Pajic, who in the ensuing period assisted me in organising the system of anti-air defences.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, if you can, I am going to ask you a question, and if you could just answer yes or no, that would be helpful. Is it correct, that at some point, in the summer of 1992, within the TO command, you were removed as head of air defence? Is that correct, sir, if so, if you could just please say yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not correct. I continued to engage in these same activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Within the staff of the TO command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also within the staff and within the joint command.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: So, if I understand you -- well, you have previously stated where there was a time where you no longer had the function of head of -- head of air defence and you became an assistant, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know whether you understand clearly the organisation and the formation of the joint command as such. If that is not clear to you, then you cannot get the real answer from me. You cannot understand me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Were you at any time removed as head of the air command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't stop performing that duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, just a few minutes ago, you testified about a point, whose date you didn't remember exactly. When you ceased having the function of head of air defence and you became an assistant; did you say that just a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You see, there are two commands. You have the joint command and then you have the command within the headquarters and the command in the HVO. My function was head of air defence in the joint command. At that time, when the joint command was formed, we had to find somebody who would perform the same duty in the municipal TO staff. In the HVO army too, they had their own head of air defence with whom I cooperated. His name was Matkovic, if that means anything to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, is it your testimony that, in the beginning, you were fulfilling the function of head of air defence for both the joint command and the TO command, and then at some point, you were relieved of your duty as head of air defence within the TO command; is that correct? Although we understand you still testify you fulfilled that duty in the joint command, but is it correct that you were removed from your function as head of air defence within the TO command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I was shown confidence and appointed to head of air defences in the joint command, my position was vacated and another person was appointed to fill in that vacancy in the municipal staff, whereas I remained an officer and the leader of the unit operating in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, has someone suggested to you that you should not answer questions with a "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Most of your witnesses are not answering questions with "yes" or "no." If he does that, why should you object?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just asked him a question. If he can answer the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: -- insist also matters explanatory to your questions. Does he not explain your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I think that he has confirmed it, but since he refuses to say "yes," I'm wondering if maybe there's something I don't understand. That's one of the reason why I ask "yes" or "no" questions so that there can be no confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He has explained what his position is and I think that should be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise Mr. Ramic's signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I would ask that this document be admitted, since the witness has recognised the signature; Prosecution Exhibit 210.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What is it meant for? What is it purported to show?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Among other things, it would show Mr. Delalic's involvement in things other than logistics and in things other than where he is serving as a witness between different parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I have not been able to see the document clearly, but it relates to civil defence, and as a coordinator, he was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If the signatures are there, that would explain that orders of the joint command, which were signed, both by the HVO and the TO commanders, which also related to some function of the war presidency, he did sign those orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it is certainly going to be up to Your Honours to determine the relevance. The Prosecution believes this document is extremely relevant, and we are prepared to argue its relevance now or later, but given that the witness has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That he signed the documents relating to some other things, other than coordinating, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I can give Your Honours extra copies, this is not a document signed by the joint command and it's not a document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But does it relate to civil defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution -- and, in fact, I would point out that the expert witnesses indicated that it did not, and these documents indicated that Mr. Delalic had a role different than either logistics or simple coordination of the war presidency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I'm just asking you, does it relate to civil defence?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution believes that this document which states, "Due to failure to follow orders, tardiness and lack of initiative while holding the post, Enver Redzepovic is relieved of duty as head of air defence and assigned to the post of air defence light artillery battery commander." The Prosecution would state that although in this time period, there is always some overlap between all military and all civilian functions, this is not consistent with a document that would normally be given to the war presidency, and for that reason we seek to have it admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object. I don't see what is the grounds for the admission of this document. The witness did not receive it. He did not confirm the truth of the contents, and all the allegations made are contrary to what has been said by witnesses. The Prosecution has already tendered this document for its limited scope and it was admitted, to a limited extent, on the basis of the expert witness, the historian. I don't see what other grounds for the admission of this document and especially through this witness if he hasn't recognised it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Are you still keen on tendering it through him. Who said he did not receive it and did not see it before now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it may be admitted on the basis that he recognised Mr. Ramic's signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Recognising somebody's signature does not make it admissible. Merely because he recognises his signature, I don't think that has anything to do with admissibility at all. I don't think it can be admitted through him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, sir, you also testified about tactical groups, and you testified that you knew where the headquarters of Tactical Group 1 were because you were present at the daily reports. Who gave the daily reports?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. The witness didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, let me just ask you: Is it the case that you testified where the headquarters of Tactical Group 1 were, and you stated that you knew that because of the daily reports; is that correct or did I misunderstand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only knew based on different kinds of stories and conversations that there was a command post, that is, that the command post of Tactical Group 1 as in Ottoman, Pazaric, Igman, Hadzici. However, I was never there. I never gave a report to the commander of the Tactical Group. I did not say anything like that so I would appreciate it if these words would not be quoted as mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Let me say, sir, that I'm trying to just state what I understood you to say. If somehow I have misunderstood or there's been a problem with interpretation, of course, I want you to correct me. If at any point I talk about something you testified about and it's not a correct representation of what you said, please, as you have just done, stop me. Now, if I understood you correctly, you testified that you never saw any orders from the supreme command appointing Mr. Delalic as commander of Tactical Group 1. My question is: Did you ever see any orders from the supreme command dealing in any way with Tactical Group 1 during the time that Mr. Delalic was commander of that Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Did you ever see any orders signed by Mr. Delalic directed to the Konjic municipal headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see those. I needed to have worked in the office in order to be able to see such documents, so this would have been the only way I could see any documents coming from the TG command to the municipal staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: During the time that Mr. Delalic was commander of Tactical Group 1, were there any soldiers from Konjic that were subordinated to him, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to what I know, we had set aside some 200 soldiers and officers for the Tactical Group 1 and they became part of that formation. I already stated that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Are these members of the Gajret unit or are these different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the Gajret unit and I was not present.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, do I understand you that there were some 2 to 300 soldiers from Konjic that were part of Tactical Group 1 during the time that Mr. Delalic was head of Tactical Group 1; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Is it correct that during the time Mr. Delalic was commander of Tactical Group 1, there were 2 to 300 soldiers from Konjic that were subordinated to Mr. Delalic, as commander of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Do you know who was the head of this unit of the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I already stated that I was not present there and I do not know exactly who it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Do you know the names of any soldiers whatsoever that were part of this group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The men who were part of the Tactical Group kept changing. It depended on the task, so after a period of time, a unit would come back to its original unit. When the Tactical Group would be tasked with a new mission, fresh troops would be set aside and appointed to it. So I don't know how many tasks and how many soldiers were there at what time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Who was it who would appoint the fresh soldiers to Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was probably the staff and staff commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Does that mean you don't know for sure, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The units numbering 2 to 300 soldiers and officers had to be approved by the municipal staff. They must have received an order from the superior command, that is, from Sarajevo, and they set aside these particular number of soldiers on the basis of the order by the republican supreme command. The municipal staff in Konjic did set aside these soldiers, and the municipal staff commander must be the person responsible for selecting and setting aside these men.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Am I correct, sir, that you believe that's the case because it's the way it should work but, in fact, you don't know how it worked in practise because you weren't involved in that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At any rate, this was the system, this is how it was done, and this is probably how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, when you inspected the Celebici barracks during the end of April 1992, was it already being used as a prison at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: During the time the Celebici prison existed, who did you understand to be commander of the prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never saw an order on the establishment of prison, nor did I take part in a meeting where an order was issued to establish a prison. Personally, I never saw any prisoners in the prison. And my duties and the scope of my work were such that I had no contact with Celebici so that I was in no position to know who established it, who was there, who commanded over the prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with me that you heard that Mr. Pavo Mucic was commander of the prison?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object at this point. She's asking this witness to speculate. He has already said he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I certainly believe I'm entitled to ask him what he heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You're entitled to ask him about rumours. That is what your position is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, given that he's a member of the joint command staff, I believe his information about who he heard was commander -- he has also stated that he only heard Delalic was commander of Tactical Group 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: He never saw the appointment ordered either, but he knows that because of his position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Are you insisting that he answer that he heard from rumours that Mucic was commander of the prison?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, given that this witness has previously given a statement in which he stated that he heard Mr. Mucic was commander of the prison, I certainly think, yes, I'm entitled to ask him about that. If he wants to say he heard it and it was rumours, well, then Your Honours may choose not to give it much weight, but certainly given that he has specifically stated that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He has already stated that he did not know about the establishment of the prison there. The other follow-up question about any commander of the prison might be unfair. He didn't know about the establishment of any prisons. Why ask him whether there was any commander of a place he did not know was established? It doesn't make sufficient sense, except in this case, I suppose. You may ask him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, did there come a time when you were aware that there was a prison in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had such information, but this was information from informal sources of local people from Konjic. Officially, I did not have this information, nor did I receive it from the persons in charge so that I would know about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with me that in addition to hearing that a prison existed, you heard that Mr. Mucic was the commander of the prison?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, I'm going to object. She's asking the witness to speculate and he has already said he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Go to your next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He has answered it sufficiently.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that you heard reports that there was mistreatment of prisoners in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When you say that I have heard a report, a report is a formal either verbal or written report which would imply that somebody has submitted the report to me, that somebody has given me a report which is not correct. This kind of pressure has -- I've already been exposed to this kind of pressure when Ms. Sabina Manke insisted that I should say something which, for instance, I was not aware of. In the end, she said, "Have you ever heard that people in the prison were mistreated?" And to such answers my response was, "I have heard about it" after people insisted, and so in response to that, I said that I had heard something to that affect.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, you stated that Mr. Delalic had no authority over Celebici. I assume from that that you know who did have authority. Please tell us the names of those persons who had authority over Celebici? If it's more than one person, feel free to give more than one name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honours. Not knowing what Zejnil's responsibility was does not imply that the witness can be asked this type of a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think the witness can answer it easily. Repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: The question is, sir: I assume from the fact that you testified that Mr. Delalic had no authority over Celebici, you have some idea of who did have authority over Celebici. I ask you to tell us the name or names of those persons who had authority over Celebici?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If he knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. I think he already stated he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You mean it follows because he doesn't know, he knows those who have authority over Celebici? That's your assumption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You're asking him complex questions. Ask him does he know who had authority, and if he says "yes," then ask him who these persons were. Don't ask complex questions which confuse the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, what are the names of those persons who had authority over Celebici?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Ask him if he knows about the authority first.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Do you know who had authority over Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know because I have never seen any document that anyone, in particular, was there, nor was I present in any of the meetings where I could have received such knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Do you know to whom the guards were subordinated?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Again, it's the same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If he knows, he can say so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's a simple, straightforward thing. When an information is not within his knowledge, he can easily say "I don't know" and that's the end of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour, but he has already stated he doesn't know anything with regard to the prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He did not mention about guards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Do you know who appointed the guards of Celebici prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Do you know to whom the guards reported or to whom they were subordinated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Can I ask that the witness be shown a copy of his prior statement?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Document 244.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you, do you recognise what has been shown to you as a copy of the statement that you gave to the office of the Prosecutor and which bears your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The statement which I signed, and this statement in the English language, this is the statement that I signed in English that is. I did not have an opportunity to sign a Bosnian language statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, I would ask that his prior statement be admitted for the sole purposes of determining the extent to which this witness has been impeached.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Which part of his statement has been impeached?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, among other things, Your Honour, for instance, I will point to the bottom of page 1 where he says, "The war had already started and we in the war presidency were permanently in contact". And then, the next paragraph, he goes on to clarify that all important people were represented in the war presidency and among them he lists the commander of the municipal TO headquarters. I'm sorry, Your Honour, I didn't hear you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: How does this mean? That it is in contradiction to what he has just said, a membership of the war presidency?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, he has stated that he was never a member of the war presidency and that, in fact, the commander of the municipal TO headquarters, was never a member.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We heard Hadzihuseinovic, and he said the membership of the war presidency was regulated by regulations and the TO and the -- and the others were not represented in that. How is this impeachment? This is exactly what he said today.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and it's also the case with respect Dr. Hadzihuseinovic -- Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, was impeached with the fact that previously he had stated that the commander of the TO was part of the war presidency. And I emphasise that the Prosecution is not saying that, in fact, under the law, the commander of the TO headquarters was or was not a member of the war presidency. The point is that is that just as -- that the persons there thought that the municipal TO commander was part of the war presidency and Mr. Hadzihuseinovic and this witness and Mr. Delalic himself all stated that initially. And we believe that is directly relevant to determining what the situation was in fact, which was confused without people always knowing what the exact provisions were. And so we believe it is absolutely, directly relevant and that's why Ms. Residovic has gotten into it in direct testimony and that's why we're allowed to impeach this witness with the fact that he stated differently on a prior occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How does it affect the matters of the case?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, you can tender it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, based on a new subject that came up during cross-examination, I request leave of court for about five minutes more. This is the second witness that has testified about some coercion in making statements. Risto Vukalo was the first one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't remember him talking about coercion. He says he might have signed the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, this man said said that Sabina Manke put words in his mouth and was pressuring him. Given the fact that another witness, a prosecution witness has suggested --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I would be surprised if an officer of his status could be classed with Sabina Manke.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I take no position on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you might, but I think very few people would take that word really seriously. Well, I don't think so. We take note of whatever. I think, if what he said is all inclusive, as against the regulations governing the appointment of members of the war presidency, well it's neither here nor there, it doesn't really affect his credibility or voracity. You might take it for all that it's worth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, given that, there's no reason to go into how this statement was made and whatever weight should be given to this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, if you have anything to say about it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may just be noted in the transcript that I objected to the proposal that you accepted and regarding the impeachment of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That you objected and the Trial Chamber felt it could be admitted. That will be -- it will be deleted. Because everything you say is recorded, so there's nothing to worry about that. It's a ruling of the Trial Chamber that I will admit it because this is a statement, without denying it, other than his explanation that he did not have the other translation, perhaps the actual translation or the language in which he made it. So for all that it is worth, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I just mentioned this because of the transcript. I am aware of your decision, thank you. However, since the Prosecutor has tendered into evidence something to impeach the witness, allow me to tender the video recording of a meeting of the municipal assembly at which this witness was proposed and which clearly shows that this witness is telling the truth. Would you allow me to show this video?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: No. Because that has nothing to do with his voracity. And it was not even challenged that he was appointed. Nobody is challenging that. Is that in issue, that he was appointed? It was not an issue that he was not nominated. None of the offices he has held have been challenged, so I don't know what your video will tell us, other than during a few minutes of a review transmission, it has nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We would gain, as Judge Jan said yesterday, evidence that supports the credibility of this witness. He was present at the session. He was proposed and elected. And it shows how, in effect, things happened in April, 1992, and not in the way it is written in this statement, whereby the Prosecutor wishes to impeach him. So this would be in support of the credibility of this witness. That is my proposal, it is up to you to judge, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I am not going to accept it, I am going to reject it. His appointment is clearly stated in evidence and there's documentary evidence in support of the facts that the war presidency proposed him and nominated him and he was appointed. So I don't see any contention given the fact that he was appointed. Now, this is a type of (inaudible) which a specific thing has been accepted. It has been accepted by credible witnesses whose evidence cannot be successfully challenged, so why do you want him to say it? It's not necessary. If you have any other questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you are confirming the credibility of this witness by what you have just said, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He's been impeached, everything will come out when all the evidence is being considered. You have no other questions? Well, I think this end of the testimony of this witness and he's accordingly discharged. Thank you very much for your assistance. Can we have your other witness now?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I call Zijad Salihamidzic as a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This is one of your Jablanica witnesses, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I'm sorry, I don't have the interpretation. I am not receiving the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He's from Jablanica municipality?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The gentleman was, for a time, in 1992, in the Jablanica municipality, commander of the Territorial Defence. And as of August, he was in Konjic, member of the staff and assistant commander for intelligence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He's expected to give evidence on the rule of Delalic in Jablanica, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The crown evidence of the Prosecution is that Delalic was the commander of all formations of a large area, including Jablanica municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That's why the consistent rejection of this theory by board Prosecution and Defence witnesses, you think it's a relevant aspect of the case you're expected to defend?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, because the superior authority is derived from this command over everything, including Celebici. That is the position of the Prosecution. You heard them arguing in response to our request for an okay, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: And the evidence of your witnesses who are inferior to the document you are relying upon, can make a difference if one takes the view the document you are referring to is taken. Well, go ahead with your witness. Go ahead with him. Swear the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. ZIJAD SALIHAMIDZIC

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, will you please introduce yourself to the court by telling us your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Zijad Salihamidzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, may I draw your attention to the fact that when you hear my question, wait for the interpretation on the headphones so that the Trial Chamber and everyone else can follow us. Have you understood me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell me, sir, when and where you were born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born on the 23rd of July, 1948, in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is your citizenship?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am a Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is your education and your occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I completed elementary school in Jablanica, secondary school for physical education in Sarajevo and the faculty for physical education at Sarajevo University.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you in April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I used to work in the district TO staff of Mostar and in 1992, I was in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When and how did you join the defence forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina and where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I had worked for a long time as the commander of the peacetime headquarters of Territorial Defence in Jablanica, ever since 1975 and until 1984, after which, due to certain abilities that I had, I was designated assistant commander of the district staff of Territorial Defence in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, some of your previous activities were certainly important for your duties in '92, but since the court is familiar with many of the facts, will you please tell us, when did you join the defence forces? After the war began, what duties you performed in the defence and where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's exactly what I am trying to tell you because the president of the Municipality of Jablanica, knowing my professional abilities, called me to an official interview in Jablanica and asked me to accept the proposal to become commander of the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence of Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who appointed you to that position in April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After this interview, the war presidency of Jablanica municipality sent the proposal to the superior command, that is the republican TO staff, and on the 16th of April, 1992, having received an appointment, the document on appointment, I became officially the commander of the Territorial Defence of Jablanica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to your personal knowledge, because you became commander of the municipal staff, who in those days appointed the TO commanders in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was an interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But who appointed you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the municipality itself, nobody appointed me. It was the republican staff of Territorial Defence that appointed me, or, rather, the ministry of defence and signed by Minister Jerko Doko and the commander of the Territorial Defence at the time Hasan Efendic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Salihamidzic, that upon arrival in The Hague, you gave to me a document, a letter of appointment that you received to the position of TO commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is my own personal document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Counsel, could this document be marked for identification? We have copies for the Trial Chamber, for the Prosecution and could it be shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is my own document, a document in my possession.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Shall we just wait for their Honours to see the document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Document 177.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, is this a document appointing you to the commander of the TO staff for the Municipality of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is my document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Since this document clearly shows how commanders were appointed and is therefore relevant and as the witness recognises it as his own, I tender it into evidence as a Defence Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Is there any objection on the part of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, who did the municipal staff of the Jablanica municipality, who was it supposed to be subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Given a normal organisation of Territorial Defence, such as existed before, the municipal TO staff should be subordinated to the district TO staff in Mostar, where I used to work as an assistant commander for morality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me whether this indeed happened?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He's wanted for morality?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe he meant morale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's morale of the forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This existed before the war, it was for ethics. I'm sorry that the translation is such that it is, I am unable to follow it. It is for ethics, not combat morale, but ethics, the word is, I'm sorry, the interpreter explains. The situation in Jablanica, is identical to the situation in Konjic, so that the witness can, as the immediate neighbour confirmed the testimony we have heard regarding similar issues, but we won't dwell on it at length. Mr. Salihamidzic, in view of the fact that the district staff in Mostar, where you used to work before the war, did not function; who was your municipal staff of Territorial Defence in Jablanica subordinated to afterwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The district staff of Territorial Defence was functioning, but it did not agree to the new organisation because the employees were exclusively Serbs and this for a short time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who then was the Jablanica municipal staff subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Jablanica Territorial Defence staff was under the direct command of the republican staff of Territorial Defence, because we accepted the suggestion of the political leadership to organise ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the moment you were appointed commander, did you begin to behave in line with the new regulations on the organisation of the armed forces of the Territorial Defence of the new state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Until when were you subordinated to the republican staff, or rather, until when were the commanders of the municipal staff appointed by the republican staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the 16th of April until the formation, I think in November of the 4th corps, we were under the direct command and control of the republican staff and we were subordinated to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were the commander of the municipal staff, was the command of Tactical Group 1, at any point in time, superior to the command of the Territorial Defence of the Municipality of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Tactical Group 1 was never superior in the sense of control and command to the Territorial Defence staff of Jablanica. And the rule is that tactical groups should be formed for a particular task and they have no authority over municipal TO staffs, in general.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were the commander of the municipal staff, did your units or part of your units from the area of Jablanica, were they transferred to the command of the tactical group, or rather, did your units participate in the tasks of that tactical group in lifting the blockade around Sarajevo at Tinovo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was the function of the tactical group. That is one particular assignment. And as the commander, I designated, I think it was 50, or I don't know the exact number now, 50 fighters, combatants, to join the tactical group which would seek to lift the blockade of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the execution of that task, did those combatants return to Jablanica and under whose command were they upon their return?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The military regulations, that as an officer I abided by, say that when my unit leaves my territory, it is subordinated to the commander of that tactical group. And upon the completion of a combat assignment, they return to their municipality, in this particular case, to my municipality, where they are appointed to the units from which they had come.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, the remainder of the army, the remaining armed formations in the territory of Jablanica municipality, who did not go to Tinovo Brdo, to become part of the tactical group, the remaining armed formations in Jablanica, under whose command were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exclusively under my command because I was the commander of the municipal staff of Territorial Defence. I commanded those forces in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Salihamidzic, how were the defence forces in Jablanica composed in those days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence and the MUP, they have a system of control and command that is separate. The MUP is accountable to the republican ministry, that is to its leader, whereas as the commander of the Territorial Defence, I was accountable to the commander of the republican TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, you said that the president of the municipality talked to you and that the war presidency agreed to propose your name before your appointment. Mr. Salihamidzic, as the commander of the Territorial Defence, were you a member of the war presidency of Jablanica municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I was the commander of the Territorial Defence and I was responsible directly to the commander of the republican TO staff. I was not accountable to the president of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, Mr. Salihamidzic, while you were a commander of the municipal staff, was the SDS arming the Serb population within the territory of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is irrelevant for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, let me address the court. Your Honours, attached to the military expert witness testimony there were a number of documents that you noticed as being exceptionally important. This witness can confirm this. And you said yourself that a witness needs it to authenticate these documents about the surrender of arms, if you can remember that part of the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We allowed you to examine this witness who is from another municipal area, just to see what the practice there was, nothing more than that. Because the practice in the municipality may be used to confirm the practice in Konjic. This you have already done.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The inhabitants of Konjic Municipality, regardless of their ethnic origin, what citizenship do they hold?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is a legal question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All the people of Konjic are Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He's not a lawyer. That's a legal question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But he knows what his citizenship is, as a fact, and of course it is up to you to judge the legal aspect. Your Honours, if you remember counts 1 and 2 of the indictment linked to Konjic, this witness will confirm the submissions of the defence and that is the attitude towards the illegally armed people and the attitude of those same people towards their own country. If I may be allowed to ask two questions from that area, I think that we shall see the reasons for the legitimate arrest and detention of those people. And these are related to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This witness will be speaking for his municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Briefly, and then I will pass on to his duties in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's his municipality he would be speaking about, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Okay, we'll break now and come back at 4.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly remind the witness that he is still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, just another question relating to your duty in the municipal staff in Jablanica. Can you tell me whether you had possession of any weapons as a staff, where was it and did you take possession of these weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I was the commander, all weapons of the Territorial Defence had previously been stored in the depots of the former JNA at Ljuta. This was in the Konjic municipality, so that my municipality, which otherwise was purchasing these weapons, never took possession of these weapons but...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After taking control of the Ljuta barracks by the defence forces of Konjic, did you eventually take possession of part of these weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I received information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You don't have to go into details.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, just in brief, if you can answer this question: After the liberation of Ljuta, did you come into possession of either all or part of the weapons there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the weapons that were found there, we received 20 per cent; 30 per cent went to Prozor and 50 per cent was received by the TO in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were these sufficient quantities of weapons or did you have to look for other places to find equipment and materiel given that you, as you stated, did not have your own weapons depots?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Given the territory that my units were securing, we had very little weapons and equipment so that my soldiers would actually leave their weapons in their front-line positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. This is enough as far as the municipal staff in Jablanica is concerned. Now, Mr. Salihamidzic, did you at one point in 1992 transfer to the municipal headquarters in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had originally come from Konjic. That's where my wife and my children were and my in-laws were there. As far as I can remember, sometime in August, I came to the TO headquarters in Konjic, and I was given a duty of an officer in the operations sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you can recall the date, that would be better, but it is fine if you just said that it was in August. Who was your commander at the municipal staff at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Mr. Esad Ramic. He was my commander when I came to the TO headquarters in Konjic, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, did you know Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was born in the village of Ostrozac which was in the Jablanica municipality. I believe he's about a year younger than I am, but I knew him from school.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the period when you were the commander of the municipal staff in Jablanica and until your arrival in Konjic, did you know what activities Mr. Zejnil Delalic was engaged in and did you have any contact with him at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I came to the municipal headquarters of the Territorial Defence of Jablanica, it was contingent on my having a uniform. You can be a soldier if you had a uniform, if you had insignia and if you had a unit. The first two uniforms I received from Mr. Zejnil Delalic. I personally received them and I put one of them on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were in the municipal headquarters of the TO in Jablanica, did Zejnil Delalic assist you with providing equipment for the needs of the municipal staff there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was very committed to doing this and thereby acquired a lot of confidence and respect of the people who had nothing. Everything that we received was very valuable for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any specific example relating to the municipal staff because the court already knows enough about his local contacts and especially with the people in Ostrozac. But was he involved in providing materiel and equipment for, for instance, a unit which went to Tinovo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. If you will allow me, this was the first operation for which I made preparation with soldiers to go there, which means that we received part of the equipment from Mr. Delalic. This is one of the specific contributions of his, to equip one of the unit which I sent out in an attempt to lift the siege of Sarajevo. This unit was placed under the command of Tactical Group 1. At that time, Mr. Mustafa Polutak, who is now a BiH army general, was the commander of Tactical Group 1 at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you came to the municipal staff in Konjic in August 1992, do you know what duty Mr. Zejnil Delalic occupied at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So this is August of 1992, and I received information that Mr. Delalic was the commander of Tactical Group 1 and that he replaced, in that position, Mr. Mustafa Polutak.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were involved in operations in a department in the municipal headquarters. Mr. Salihamidzic, was the commander of the Tactical Group 1, Mr. Zejnil Delalic, a superior officer to you or to anyone in the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The hierarchy was identical as the one in Jablanica. The municipal staff commands and controls -- its commander, that is, commands and controls its own units in its own area of responsibility, and the commander of the tactical unit receives a specific tactical task which is limited by the time in which it is to be executed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, is it correct that after your arrival in The Hague, you gave me a chart detailing the organisation of the territorial municipal staff of 1992 and that you have a copy of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I found this chart among my documents from the period when I was in the operations department, and this chart also contains names of officers who were in certain positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: With the usher's assistance, can I have this document distributed and then also marked for identification? There are enough copies for the court here.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence document D178/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, can you please show where your position was in August, according to this chart?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the left-hand side, it says "Staff," and then down the line of command "Chief of staff, assistant chief of staff for operations and training," and then following that, several officers among whom my name also appears as officer for operations and tactical affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, since the witness is in possession of this document and he recognised his own position in the municipal staff, I move to admit it into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Did he himself prepare this chart?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. As we heard, this was a chart which was in the headquarters when he was a member there. That was in August of 1992. I'm just repeating what the witness has testified to. I cannot testify on his behalf. You will also recall, Your Honours, that Witness Cerovac recreated from memory a similar chart, and I think that it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Cerovac is in a higher position and he is in a better position to talk about it. This officer is not in a similar position and, strictly speaking, cannot himself -- apart from the fact that if his name appears, yes, but that doesn't mean that it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I think this is identical with another document which we had admitted previously. It is your decision, Your Honours. You have heard the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Then rely on the document that has already been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's already in evidence. If it is identical with what Cerovac spoke about here, why do you want to bring in this again? Is his name not in the other list?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, Cerovac produced the documents based on his memory of it in 1998. This is a document from 1992 which is in possession of this witness. It supports the chart that Cerovac produced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He was chief of staff in 1992 in the municipal army there. That's a more authentic document than this one. It's not necessary. You can carry on with your evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, did you take over other duties in this staff at one point and, if you did, can you tell the court which ones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was indisposed very briefly, and sometime in late August, early September, I was given a duty of the assistant deputy for intelligence. I believe that my superior officer Mr. Cerovac and the commander had followed my work and had assigned me to that post.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask Mr. Salihamidzic some questions and I would like to ask the witness a question relating to D145 A5 D/39 or in the transcript page 807. I have the copies prepared for the court so can the witness please be shown this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, was this a document which appoints you to assistant deputy officer for intelligence in the municipal headquarters in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the document signed by my commander, Mr. Esad Ramic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I move to admit this document as a Defence exhibit. Mr. Salihamidzic, when you became assistant chief for intelligence, what were your basic duties in this position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had a short period of preparation while I was still an operations officer and then I transferred to this duty. My basic duty as assistant to chief of intelligence was to collect information based on intelligence and recognisance, information that is on the aggressor, that was the basic duty and task of assistant the chief. And after the relevant information was collected, I submitted it to my chief for further use in connection with preparations for anticipated combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In answer to one of my questions, you said that tactical group always bound to a particular task, Mr. Salihamidzic, did you have any duties in providing intelligence information to tactical groups in the areas towards Sarajevo, and if yes, based on what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since I have certain military knowledge, expertise and I had worked in a much larger size command and I know what it means to conduct certain combat operations, the rule is that a tactical group which has not been -- which is not fully fledged, that such tactical group should be supplied with intelligence. Because when a tactical group is in the process of performing a task, it has to have the information regarding the front lines where the task is performed, the flanks and, of course, the depth of the area in which it is engaged.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Apart from your general knowledge, did you also have any documents, such as order or a directive from another command which would further specify what your duties were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We forwarded our -- all information to our centre for intelligence and this intelligence centre for the purposes of our better operating sent us a directive--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually what is all of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --in order to better perform or combat duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What is he trying to show?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I wish to show that this witness had certain obligations in relation to the tactical group in executing his duties as a citizen for intelligence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: So what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The centre which sent that information to the persons concerning, how is that relevant for our purpose? You have taken fifteen minutes already.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, among the evidence admitted is a document that has to do with intelligence data. And this is the only person that this document of Zejnil Delalic's could have been addressed to and I want this witness to tell us whether he had any basis for collecting such data in conveying them to Tactical Groups. Not only Tactical Group 1, but also Tactical Group 2, which are in the front lines and which have no developed services of their own. And this is what the witness has just told us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Instead of going through all that, he could have said that it was part of my duty to supply information and the supplying of information to Zejnil Delalic didn't mean that he was my superior. You could have asked him instead of going the round about way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, for teaching me how to put my questions, but it is not my practice --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I am not teaching you anything, I know that you know more than anybody else probably in this chamber. But then, please, be direct and ask him his duty to Tactical Group 1. I am not teaching you, because you know more, I suppose, than anybody else here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
