utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, did you ever have the duty to supply intelligence data to Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as the commander of the tactical group and even to the commander of Tactical Group 2 because they were responsible for the security of all our areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you personally, physically carry such data to the command of Tactical Group 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since Mr. Dinko Zebic from the HVO structure worked in this field also, we went together to Pazaric on one occasion where we exchanged such data and gave them for use.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, this obligation of yours, to submit such reports to the commander of Tactical Group 1, or rather to the command of that group, did it emanate from any document of your superior command, that is the republican staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had instructions which made it obligatory on us to supply units which do not have such developed services of their own, such data, so that they would be successful in combat and so that they would be able to achieve their goal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Counsel, may Prosecution Exhibit 224 be shown to the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: What is this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please place the English version on the ELMO. I don't have copies of this document because it has already been admitted as Prosecution Exhibit. Could you please put the English version on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you read the document? Just a moment, please, the document cannot be seen on the ELMO, could the usher please assist? It is the question of the development of the reconnaissance unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This document dated 14th November, when Mr. Delalic is about to wind-up and leave the country?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention, Mr. Salihamidzic, to Point 6 of this document, which I hope you have managed to read. Can it be shown on the ELMO, can we see the second page, so that the Trial Chamber can see what it's about? The signatory of that document obliges the municipal staffs to supply certain data. Tell me, Mr. Salihamidzic, have you turned the document to page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: THE USHER
utterances.text: There's only one page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's in there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please read Point 6 so that we can see how it reads because we can't see it on the ELMO. Point 6 is not on page 1, I'm sorry, I can't see the English text. Does this point establish the responsibility and duty of municipal commanders in relation to the person who issued this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was our obligation to provide such intelligence data and this is identical to the instructions we received from our superior command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true then that previously, in order with the instructions of the superior command, you were obliged to supply tactical groups with those data?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is a rule, and we had instructions to that effect. This is a military rule.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, do those instructions and this order have anything to do with the Celebici prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was wondering why you were showing me this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because I am talking about military things.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, so that is an indirect answer that there is no connection?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is right, there is none. Do you know Mr. Jerko Kostic, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had said that I had lived in Mostar with my family after 1984 and I know that Jerko Kostic from Mostar, because he worked in the state security service.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in Konjic in August, 1992, did you meet this man and do you know what his duties were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, not just once, but on a number of occasions, later, I met Mr. Jerko and we talked. He was sent from Mostar to Konjic to assist the HVO --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I learned that through conversations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Jerko Kostic ever ask you to provide him with certain data?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On a number of occasions. His sphere of interest was the retired General Jovan Dijak. He particularly insisted on data about him. And since Mr. Dijak was my commander --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us leave that aside. Did he ask you for any other data and what position did he hold at the time he asked you for this data?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time he was in SIS, the intelligence service of the HVO. And, probably, these data were needed by that service. And knowing the purpose and possible use of those data and the data referred to a senior military officer in the BiH army, information which could be compromising, I would not supply such data.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he ever ask you for information about Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but he didn't insist so much on those.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me, please, after Zejnil Delalic left Konjic, did the HVO launch a fierce campaign against Mr. Delalic and Mr. Dijak as being members of the intelligence service of the former Yugoslav army, are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is hard for me to talk about this, but there were all kinds of rumours about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We won't go into the rumours, but if you have any personal knowledge about these things, it is much more important than any rumours or stories you may have heard. Do you have any personal knowledge about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You see, that is the way how to obtain information. That is how you do obtain information. You hear this here and something else there, and that's how you collect information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question is, at the time were you able to follow the media who were fiercely attacking Zejnil Delalic and Mr. Jovan Dijak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions on behalf of the witness, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a few.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: May it please the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir, my name is Tom Moran, and I think I have spoken to you just briefly and I represent a man named Hazim Delic. And I want to ask you a few questions, but the first question I want to ask, I think is a question on the minds of a lot of people in this courtroom, what exactly does the assistant commander for morality do in an army unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have two specialities. One is control and command and the other is morality. I prefer the latter one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: What are your duties, sir, as a morality officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you have the patience to hear me out, I should like to give you an example to show you and then it's up to you to judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: If you could give us the short version, sir, I think at least some of the court, and I know I was just curious of what a morality officer is, because in armies I'm familiar with, there's no such title, no such person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Is it really important?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: It's just interesting, Judge, but we can go on to something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Sir, when you were answering questions from Ms. Residovic, you were talking about the weapon shortage, I believe, while you were the commander in Jablanica, and something came out translated and on the transcript and I didn't understand it, and so I'm going to just see if I can clarify it in my own mind. You said something about weapons were so short that you would leave them in front-line positions. By that, sir, did you mean that when one soldier would leave a front-line position and another one would replace him in that position that there were so few weapons that the man coming to the front took the weapon from the man going to the rear? Sir, you have to say "yes" or "no" because there's a lady over hear called a court reporter and she has to write down everything we say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Another thing you said while you were talking to Ms. Residovic was something along the lines, and I just have a few notes on it, is that you were a soldier if you had a uniform and an insignia. Does that mean, sir, that people who did not have a uniform and did not have an insignia were not soldiers and were not to be treated like soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't quite get your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir, and that's good. If you have a problem understanding one of my questions, have me stop and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll answer as soon as you repeat the question once again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. As I recall, you told Ms. Residovic or you said that you were a soldier if you had a uniform and insignia; do you remember telling her that or did I just take bad notes on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You see, according to international law, and you are an expert in the field, I am not, but as far as I know, a soldier is a person wearing a uniform, the insignia of a soldier, an indication of the unit he belongs to and the command he belongs to. That is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I just wanted to make sure that I was clear in my mind about that, sir. One last area and then I think I'll be done. Sir, you've been both a commander and a staff officer. I'm going to ask you a little bit about the differences in authority that come with those two different status’s. Sir, would it be fair to say that a commander, by virtue of his legal status as a commander, has the personal authority to order his subordinates, the people in his unit, to perform legal tasks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Legal tasks?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir, legal duties.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Legal duties in the sense of carrying out a certain combat task, combat assignment, if I understood you well?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir, or for that matter to wash dishes after dinner or whatever; a legal duty (sic) has the right to order his subordinates to carry out functions related to that unit and, so long as those orders are legal orders, require his subordinates to follow them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are placing a lot of emphasis on legality and law and I'm a military man. I would prefer to answer a more simple question. I apologise for not being able to answer this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That's fair, sir. The reason I say "legal orders" is I don't want anyone to think that I'm suggesting that a commander has the right to order his troops to work at Auschwitz or anything like that. What I'm saying is if it's a legal order, legal under your national law, legal under international law, that a commander has the personal authority to order his subordinates to follow those orders, and that if they fail to follow those orders, he has the personal authority to punish them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If a commander issues an order, it has to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And that's because the commander has the personal right to issue those orders by virtue of his position as commandant, as commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And people who are not commanders, staff officers, deputy commanders, people like that, they only have the authority to issue orders which are given to them by the commander; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They have their own competencies because they are of a lower rank and they have their own terms of reference which are regulated by rules and regulations regarding the service under various conditions. Is it guard duty or some other obligations or duties that are important?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, but they don't have the same kind of power to command and punish that a commander does, do they, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is a rule on military discipline, rules of military discipline. According to those rules, every commanding officer has to act any officer in command so that if a soldier carries out an offence or makes an error, it is exactly stated what the punishment is. Nothing is left to chance. Everything is regulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Sir, what I'm getting at is it's the commander that applies those regulations, not the operations officer or the deputy commander or the chief of staff. It's the commander that has the legal responsibility and the legal power to do that; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the commander is the most responsible person in the control and command of a particular unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: In fact, the commander is responsible for everything his unit does or fails to do; isn't that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honour, I'll pass the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any other questions, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might, I have not had a chance to visit with this witness very long, and if I could just have a moment in the morning, I may have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If you have any questions, please ask them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: No. I don't have any at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any questions by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Salihamidzic. My name is Giuliano Turone, and I am attorney for the Prosecution and I would like to ask you a limited number of questions, if you don't mind. I will focus, at least for the moment, on the period when you went to Konjic after August 1992. You said that you joined the TO staff in August 1992, and later on we saw the appointing document of 16 September, '92, the Konjic municipal staff appointed you to perform the duty of deputy staff head for the intelligence service in the army staff of Konjic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had two appointments. One was the appointment for operations and tactical affairs and the other was for intelligence affairs, and I think that you have seen those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I just wanted to remember the area. In this capacity of yours within the Konjic municipality, the first one in August and the second one as intelligence officer, did you get to know who had a position of superiority regarding prisons in the territory of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was not something I inquired into. It was not my area of interest as an intelligence officer. My area of interest were the enemy territories --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I know quite well that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- which means the front, so that my interest could not focus on something at hand. That was not of any interest to me as an intelligence officer. That didn't interest me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I understand that and I accept it quite well; I have no difficulty with that. But I'm just asking you, since you were, in any case, an officer, a military with the higher rank in the municipality and you had an --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I object, Your Honours. The witness has said that he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I would like to be allowed to finish my further question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Put the question to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I take it that it is not your field of interest. But since you were an officer for intelligence services and you had, I take it, a wide knowledge of the military situation in the municipality of Konjic, my question is whether you did, in any case, get any information whatsoever about the persons who might have had a position of superiority regarding prisons in the area of Konjic? If you have no idea whatsoever, you can just answer that you do not know. But if you had a chance to get indirectly any information, even if that was not the real field of your interests, please tell us if you had any information like that, if you got to know something like that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I engaged in intelligence matters for a very brief period of time. I think it was a period of one month. There was constant shelling and preparations for combat. My prime responsibility was to collect as much information as possible from others. I am not able to give you a concrete answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Turone, I think we will stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We will resume tomorrow morning at 10 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you. We will resume tomorrow at ten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 26th day of May, 1998 at 10.00 a.m.
